- Model consistently underestimates prices in early days of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes in recent history (e.g., after 88.85 or 90.01), often overshooting by 1–3 points.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), failing to capture mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends.
- Model exhibits overconfidence in short-term volatility, producing erratic peaks and troughs that don’t align with actual price smoothing.
- When history includes a recent high, model often fails to adjust downward sufficiently, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model underreacts to low-price periods, failing to anticipate sharp drops when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to be overly optimistic in the first 3–5 days, then gradually adjusts — suggesting a delayed correction mechanism.
